model_annotation: Figure 4, titled "DISTRIBUTION OF SAMPLES (%) ACROSS VARYING VALUES OF SAMPLE-LEVEL AMBIGUITY STANDARD DEVIATION AND SAMPLE-LEVEL MAXIMUM AMBIGUITY," is a scatter plot that visualizes the distribution of samples based on two metrics. The horizontal axis represents "Ambiguity Std" (sample-level ambiguity standard deviation), and the vertical axis represents "Max Ambiguity" (sample-level maximum ambiguity). The plot displays a collection of data points, each corresponding to a sample, with their positions determined by their respective standard deviation and maximum ambiguity values. The data points are distributed across the plot, showing a general trend where samples with higher standard deviation tend to also have higher maximum ambiguity, though there is considerable spread. The caption and surrounding text indicate that this figure is used to illustrate how different ambiguity scenarios are categorized as "most ambiguous," "dear," "somewhat ambiguous," or "very ambiguous" based on these two metrics.
